_: A GENERIC MINECRAFT LOOP FILE: one session authors one block model - geometry and texture in
Blockbench, exported into the mod's resources, pushed into the running game and looked at.
Copy THIS FILE and check-block-model.mjs beside it into <your mod>/.mcptoolkit/ as loop.json
and check-block-model.mjs, leave MCPTK_PROFILE unset so the session launches in this profile,
and edit both until they are your project's rules. docs/guides/LOOPS.md is the walkthrough;
mcp-server/loop/loop.mjs is the schema and the checker contract.
THE CHECK RUNS WHERE ITS SUBJECT IS. A `run` check is a command on the FILESYSTEM, and the
filesystem only learns about the model when export_model writes it - so this one fires after
export_model rather than after every edit, and reads exactly what was just written. That makes
the loop's rhythm export-early-export-often, which is the right habit anyway: the exported json
is what the game loads. A loop that wants a report on EVERY editing reply needs the other form,
an `eval` check, which runs inside Blockbench through risky_eval and can read the live project;
loop.mjs documents it and there is no file for it to go stale against.
THE GATE IS ON push_asset, NOT ON export_model. Gating the tool that FEEDS the check deadlocks:
the exported model has a problem, the fix is in Blockbench, and clearing the problem needs
another export - which the gate would refuse. So the gate sits on the next act instead, which
is also the one worth guarding: a broken model does not go into the running game. Nothing is
gated until the check has run once; a session that never exports has nothing standing.
THE KEEP-LIST IS PRICED. Every name here is paid on EVERY turn of the session, so it is the
whole cost lever (LOOP_KIT_DESIGN.md section 11.2). This is `art` minus what a block model has
no use for: `animation` (a block model has no keyframes), `stage_entity` and `launch_game` and
`get_log` and `list_assets` and `render`, and the seven mem_* tools. `trigger_action` is absent
for a different reason - `art` excludes it on purpose (driving the app's UI blind is a fallback,
not a pipeline) and profile.keep is ABSOLUTE rather than a filter over its base, so listing it
here would quietly put it back. Every other name below is served by `art` today; a name that is
not warns on the shim's stderr, and a REAL tool this list omits is silent, so re-read it against
the manifest when the surface moves. probes/loop-examples.test.mjs is what keeps this one honest.
WHAT THE CHECKER DOES NOT SEE. It reads the exported json and the PNG files it names: element
bounds and rotations, face and uv legality, texture variables that resolve, sheets that exist.
It cannot see the blockstate that points at the model, the block's registration, the language
entry, or whether the thing looks right - that last one is what the pictures are for, and the
budget below is small on purpose because every picture is re-sent on every later turn.

notes.project: Start a block with op:new {format:"java_block", texture_width:16, texture_height:16}, which also binds it to this session; op:save writes the .bbmodel you keep beside the mod, and it is not what the game loads.
notes.place_cube: A block model's cubes live in 0..16 on every axis - that is the block itself - and Minecraft refuses anything outside -16..32. Leave `group` alone unless the model needs bones; a block model has no bones.
notes.create_texture: 16x16 for one block face's worth of pixels; a sheet whose height is a multiple of its width is read by the game as an ANIMATION strip and needs a .mcmeta beside it.
notes.paint_faces: Whole faces by "<cube>.<face>", one call for all of them. Paint moves with the faces when a cube is resized, so paint after the geometry settles.
notes.export_model: This is what the game loads, and it is what the check reads: export_model {codec:"java_block", path:"src/main/resources/assets/<namespace>/models/block/<name>.json"}. Export whenever the geometry changes - the check is the only thing that sees the file.
notes.push_asset: Puts the exported json and the PNG into the RUNNING game; follow it with reload_resources. Refused while the last check left problems standing, unless you pass force:"<why>".

profile.instructions: Blockbench is open and this session is authoring ONE Minecraft block model. Bind a project first (`project op:new {format:"java_block"}` for a new one, `op:open {path}` for an existing .bbmodel) and touch no other tab. Model in block coordinates: 0..16 on every axis is the block, +Y is up, and the game refuses an element outside -16..32. Geometry first, then the texture, then look. `export_model {codec:"java_block", path:...}` writes what the game actually loads, and every export's reply ends with the block's check - fix what it names before moving on. `push_asset` into the running game is refused while problems stand unless you force it with a reason.
